title: incident-bot: add /audit-export status command (backlog + connector errors)
author: Rafael Mendes
body:
Context: During recent staging/prod exercises we lost time triaging audit-export lag because the first steps were always “find the right dashboard”, “figure out which destination(s) are impacted”, and “is the backlog growing or just delayed?”. This PR adds a first-pass triage command to incident-bot so on-call can get export status in Slack in <30s.

What’s in this PR: Adds a new Slack command `/audit-export status` that queries the audit-export control plane health endpoint and renders a compact summary by destination: overall state, backlog estimate, last_success_at, last_error (with classification), and a hint when the error pattern matches common connector issues (auth/403, throttling/429, 5xx, schema/validation). Includes optional flags: `--workspace <slug|id>` (required), `--destination <id>` (optional narrow), `--env hosted|dedicated|private` (defaults to hosted), `--verbose` (includes last_error_id + retry/DLQ counters if present).

Behavior/details: The command calls `GET /v1/audit-export/destinations:status` via the existing internal service client, with on-behalf-of + bot identity headers. The response is already available from ENG-13928 work; this PR just surfaces it in Slack with sane formatting. If the endpoint returns partial status (e.g., connector timeout), we still return what we have and mark the destination row as “unknown/partial” rather than failing the whole command.

Security: We gate the command behind the same incident-bot role check as other operational commands (SRE-oncall + Security Eng oncall). The command output intentionally excludes secrets and raw error payloads. For Private deployments, we only display status if the workspace has Private connectivity configured for the bot; otherwise we return a clear error with next steps.

Testing: Unit tests for formatting + error classification, plus an integration-style test using a mock audit-export status endpoint. Added snapshot coverage for the Slack block kit rendering.

Rollout: This is additive and hidden behind `INCIDENT_BOT_ENABLE_AUDIT_EXPORT_STATUS=true` initially. After merge, we’ll enable in #oncall-sre and #eng-security first, then roll out globally once we confirm no unexpected traffic patterns.

Related: ENG-13931 (dashboards/alerts), ENG-13928 (status fields), and recent lag report in SUP-23129.

Screenshots (Slack): Example output:
- Workspace: acme-prod (hosted)
- Destinations: splunk-main (degraded, backlog 182k, last_success 12m ago, last_error=HEC_5XX), s3-archive (ok, backlog 0)

Follow-ups (not in this PR): Add “pause destination” shortcut (control-plane write), and a “replay window” helper once ENG-13934 lands.

review_conversation:
Sean Gallagher: Can we make sure the command doesn’t page the audit-export service by accident (i.e., no aggressive retries)? Also please add clear messaging for partial responses.

Rafael Mendes (author): Good call. Limited to 1 retry with jittered backoff (200–400ms) and a hard 2s total timeout. Partial responses now render with a “partial” badge and we include the error in a footer.

Allison Grant: Formatting looks good. Can we include a quick hint when we detect the common Splunk HEC 5xx pattern (likely upstream) vs our own auth issues? Also please avoid dumping huge error strings into Slack.

Rafael Mendes (author): Added classification + short hints (e.g., “Upstream 5xx from sink; consider pausing destination if backlog > threshold”). Error strings are truncated to 160 chars and we only show `error_id` under `--verbose`.

Ethan Park: API call path looks right but for Private env this will fail unless the bot can reach the tenant’s control plane. Please make the error actionable.

Rafael Mendes (author): Added explicit message: “Private env status unavailable: no bot connectivity configured for this workspace” and linked internal runbook section.

Sean Gallagher: Approved after the retry/timeout changes. Please keep the feature flag default-off until we verify volume.

Allison Grant: Approved.

Ethan Park: Approved.
